messages:
jamie: Heads-up — weekend coverage looking light. I'm primary Fri 18:00-23:59, but I have a calendar conflict Sat morning. Need to lock secondary coverage and a shadow for new joiner @taylor.

ashley: I can take Sat 00:00-08:00 primary if needed. Is primary->secondary handoff every 4 hours or when we see a paging spike?

casey: We normally do fixed shifts: primary handles pages, secondary watches for escalations and looks at runbook steps. Handoffs at top-of-hour ok. For this weekend can do 08:00-16:00 primary.

jamie: Perfect. Plan: jamie primary Fri 18:00-23:59, ashley primary Sat 00:00-08:00, casey primary Sat 08:00-16:00, srini on-call Sun 00:00-08:00 (will confirm). Secondary rota: ashley covers Fri night as secondary, taylor will shadow casey Sat morning.

taylor: happy to shadow. What's the onboarding play? any pre-read?

casey: Taylor — check runbook: https://confluence.redwood/allhands/oncall-runbook (links in thread). Key bits: 
1) Pagerduty escalation flow (ack -> investigate -> triage -> engage SRE).
2) Quick triage checklist (service, error rate, customer impact).
3) Rollback steps for model-serving infra.

casey: Quick snippet to save: 
```
# quick triage
curl -sS https://health.internal/api/status | jq .
kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | grep model-server
# if >50% errors -> run rollback-job
```

devops-bot: Incident rule triggered: high 5xx rate on /v1/generate for eu-west. Alert ID: INC-2026-4521. Timestamp: 1719007000

jamie: saw the bot. I'm going to run the quick triage now. @ashley please stand by as secondary.

ashley: standing by. :eyes:

jamie: Triage notes: 5xx spike localized to two nodes (g4dn-8x). Logs show OOMs and kernel churn. Customer impact: some tail-latency spikes and ~0.8% failed requests for hosted API. Not a full outage but visible to clients.

casey: Do we have mitigation in runbook for OOM? I can trigger a rotator to move traffic off those nodes.

jamie: Yes — runbook section "evacuate node". Steps: 
1) cordon node with kubectl
2) scale up replacement pod pool (deploy tmp-variant)
3) move routing weight to healthy pool (via router --set-weight)

jamie: Executing cordon now: 
```
kubectl cordon node/g4dn-8x-02
kubectl drain node/g4dn-8x-02 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

incident-bot: Action logged: node cordoned by jamie at 1719007289.

ashley: After cordon, I pushed a temporary increased pool: `infractl scale inference-pool --replicas 6 --region eu-west` — should reduce pressure.

srini: Quick question for shadowing: taylor — can you watch the scaling steps in Console? I'll walk you through the routing weight toggle when we do the handoff.

taylor: watching screenshare now. saw the drain logs. learning a lot, thanks.

casey: traffic back to normalish, 5xx now ~0.1%. Customer impact reduced. Recommend keep monitoring for 1 hour then handoff as planned.

jamie: Agreed. I'll note mitigation in incident doc and hand off to ashley at 23:59. Taylor — after handoff, try the post-incident checklist (notify customers if degraded SLAs, attach incident timeline).

ashley: I'll take over at 23:59. For handoff protocol remind: primary writes a 1-paragraph summary + actions taken and open followup tickets.

jamie: Copy. Summary (to paste into incident doc): "Localised OOMs on two eu-west nodes caused transient 5xx spike (~0.8% request failures). Actions: cordoned nodes, drained pods, scaled replacement pool, rerouted traffic. Result: errors fell to ~0.1%. Follow-ups: investigate root cause (kernel OOM vs model memory regression), add pre-scaling alarm at 0.5% error rate, tag faulted nodes for forensic logs."

taylor: added shadow notes to onboarding doc. can I be listed as shadow for next weekend too? would like another ride.

casey: yes, we'll pair again. Also adding a small checklist for shadows: 
- sit with primary during triage
- follow runbook steps in staging first
- note questions for postmortem

jamie: OK closing out here. Thanks team — excellent quick mitigation. If anything flares I'll @channel. :party-parrot:
